Thought: Aldehydes contain a carbonyl group (C=O) with at least one hydrogen atom attached to the carbon. When exposed to air (which contains oxygen), aldehydes are susceptible to oxidation. In this oxidation process, the aldehyde group (-CHO) is converted to a carboxylic acid group (-COOH). This is a well-known reaction in organic chemistry. Aldehydes are more easily oxidized than ketones because of the hydrogen attached to the carbonyl carbon. This oxidation can occur slowly at room temperature when aldehydes are exposed to air over time.

Let me check each option:
A. They isomerize to ketones - No, this is not what typically happens. Isomerization would involve rearrangement of atoms, not oxidation.
B. They oxidize to carboxylic acids - Yes, this is correct. Aldehydes readily oxidize to form carboxylic acids when exposed to air (oxygen).
C. They polymerize - While some aldehydes can polymerize under certain conditions, this is not the primary reaction that occurs when simply exposed to air.
D. They reduce to alcohols - No, exposure to air would cause oxidation (loss of electrons), not reduction (gain of electrons).
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
